items.title: Fake “View & Sign” and Adobe Acrobat Lures Deliver Attacker-Configured ScreenConnect Clients
items.summary:
CloudSEK researchers uncovered fake Adobe Acrobat and “View & Sign” pages distributing legitimate, digitally signed ConnectWise ScreenConnect installers configured for unauthorized remote access. The campaign uses Telegram bots to track visitors, profiles devices and networks, and automatically downloads remote-access clients. The findings highlight how attackers can weaponize trusted software to potentially gain persistent access to Windows systems, bypassing traditional security checks based on file signatures.
Authors : Gagan Aggarwal

items.title: The Doorway Botnet: Inside a Large-Scale IoT and Network Device Compromise Campaign
items.summary:
Thousands of routers, surveillance cameras, and enterprise servers are being exploited in a global botnet operation known as Doorway. CloudSEK’s investigation uncovered 41 GB of exposed operational data, revealing 59 exploit modules, automated credential attacks, and sophisticated malware delivery mechanisms. With 11,363 device joins recorded in a single hour, the investigation exposes how cybercriminals systematically compromise devices and build proxy infrastructure at scale.
Authors : Lakshya Dubey

items.title: Inside "MR ROBOT" - Anatomy of a Malware-as-a-Service Operation Targeting Indian Bank Customers
items.summary:
A new Android malware operation called MR ROBOT is turning banking fraud into a subscription business. CloudSEK’s investigation reveals how cybercriminals rent customised banking trojans to steal OTPs, card details, UPI PINs and credentials while secretly forwarding calls to bypass security checks. One tracked affiliate intercepted 5,407 SMS messages across 153 infected devices, exposing the scale of this Malware-as-a-Service operation targeting Indian bank customers.
Authors : Bhavik Malhotra

items.title: NEBULA - Seven Fake AI SDK Packages on npm Install a Windows RAT That Needs No DLL
items.summary:
CloudSEK uncovered NEBULA, a malicious npm supply-chain campaign involving seven fake AI SDK packages distributed through four attacker-controlled accounts. Disguised as legitimate developer tools, these packages deploy a modified KNTRAT Windows trojan capable of stealthy remote access, camera and microphone surveillance, and persistence. The investigation reveals advanced syscall-based evasion techniques, active threats, and actionable indicators for security teams.
Authors : Vikas Kundu

items.title: Caught in 4K: The Gentlemen Files
items.summary:
A Russian-speaking Gentlemen ransomware affiliate called Azazel robbed two dozen victims across six countries, then double-crossed his own gang by publishing the loot on a private leak site and pocketing every dollar. CloudSEK traced 50TB of exposed infrastructure and a live AI-driven attack chain. Read how "Caught in 4K" cracked the operation.
Authors : CloudSEK TRIAD

items.title: MALFEX - A malicious npm postinstall no advisory has caught for fourteen months
items.summary:
CloudSEK uncovered MALFEX, a long-running npm supply-chain campaign linked to a single operator, using malicious packages to deploy RATs and credential stealers. Two packages remain installable, including one malicious postinstall that evaded advisories for 14 months.
Authors : Vikas Kundu

items.title: TOPHIT Part 2: Renting the Attack Surface
items.summary:
CloudSEK found an attacker's control panel targeting vast.ai, a GPU rental marketplace. It rents containers beside victims to scan their networks. It reached one unprotected notebook and planted no miners. The panel exposed its own source code.
Authors : Vikas Kundu

items.title: TOPHIT Part 1: A one-operator npm typosquat flood, co-hosted with a GPU-cryptojacking C2
items.summary:
CloudSEK found 85 malicious npm packages, published in three minutes, likely named to surface in search when developers mistype popular libraries. They give attackers remote command access. The same server hosts a GPU-hijacking panel. No victims confirmed.
Authors : Vikas Kundu

items.title: GHAPPIER - One loader, sixty-five repositories, twenty-two accounts: an unreported loader family beside DPRK's PolinRider campaign
items.summary:
CloudSEK researchers uncovered GHAPPIER, a previously unreported loader operation spanning at least 65 public repositories, 73 infected files and 22 accounts. The investigation began with a compromised legitimate npm package whose malicious release carried valid provenance through trusted publishing. The report maps the wider infrastructure, links parts of the activity to the PolinRider campaign, and details indicators, attack flow and defensive actions.
Authors : Vikas Kundu

items.title: Tracking BigBear 2.0 Evilginx2 Phishing Campaign
items.summary:
CloudSEK researchers uncovered BigBear 2.0, a global Microsoft 365 phishing-as-a-service operation targeting hundreds of organizations across 40+ countries. The investigation exposed the attacker’s admin panel, affiliate network, phishing infrastructure, and thousands of stolen credentials and session cookies, revealing how modern AiTM attacks can hijack authenticated sessions even after MFA.
Authors :

items.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
items.summary:
The first in CloudSEK's "Caught in 4K" series, where we pull ransomware operations out of the shadows and show exactly how they work. A misconfigured server opened a window straight into an Aurora ransomware operator's playbook: attacker tools, AI-assisted planning, and a look inside the actual negotiation panel where a victims and the operator settled on payment. In partnership with TRM Labs, we traced that payment on-chain, into a wider laundering network moving money across multiple victims. This is what ransomware looks like from the inside.
Authors : CloudSEK TRIAD

items.title: BRIDGEHEAD : An npm typosquatting campaign that crosses from WSL into Windows to plant a crypto-wallet stealer
items.summary:
CloudSEK’s BRIDGEHEAD investigation exposes a 40-package npm typosquatting campaign that abuses WSL to reach Windows hosts and deploy a concealed Rust-based stealer. The malware targets cryptocurrency wallets, browser credentials, cookies and Telegram sessions, while executing largely in memory and using public infrastructure for reconnaissance and exfiltration, making detection and takedown significantly harder.
Authors : Vikas Kundu

items.title: AI-Agent-Driven Offensive Operation : Exposed Adversary Open Directory Reveals Autonomous Crypto-Theft Campaign Leading to Mass Wallet and Credential Compromise
items.summary:
CloudSEK uncovered a Chinese-speaking threat operator using autonomous AI coding agents to scale cyberattacks, including mass WordPress compromise, cryptocurrency wallet theft, credential harvesting and cryptojacking. The exposed infrastructure also revealed a developing blockchain-based command-and-control system designed to make future operations more resilient to takedowns.
Authors : Ayush Panwar

items.title: LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack: 2,500+ Companies Exposed in the Largest AI Supply Chain Breach of 2026
items.summary:
CloudSEK's research on the LiteLLM supply chain attack, the largest AI supply chain breach of 2026, names the organizations potentially exposed: 2,500+ companies and 434,000 CI/CD pipelines worldwide. The LiteLLM breach began with a compromised Trivy build and cascaded through PyPI into automated CI/CD pipelines, putting cloud credentials, source code repositories, Kubernetes environments and AI infrastructure at risk. Check whether your domain appears in the exposure dataset.
Authors :

items.title: TXTBOOK A Supply Chain Heist, Rehearsed in Public
items.summary:
A Dependency Confusion Campaign Against Tinkoff Bank's Private Package Namespace
Authors :

items.title: Access For Sale: Inside a Russian-Speaking Access Broker's Dual Operation
items.summary:
CloudSEK researchers uncovered an exposed server linked to a Russian-speaking initial access broker, revealing months of operations targeting internet-facing infrastructure across multiple sectors. The investigation connects credential theft, Active Directory compromise, and access sales to ransomware groups, while also uncovering surveillance activity targeting Ukrainian defence and aerospace organizations.
Authors : CloudSEK TRIAD

items.title: Tax Season, Open Season: Phishing and Malware Campaigns Targeting Indian Taxpayers
items.summary:
A tax-season malware campaign is impersonating the Income Tax Department, sending fake penalty notices over WhatsApp. Victims who tap "Download Documents" install malware capable of harvesting OTPs and banking credentials. The advisory also covers a wider ecosystem of refund SMS fraud, cloned e-Filing portals, and fake e-PAN emails targeting Indian taxpayers this season.
Authors : Shobhit Mishra

items.title: France Cyber Threat Outlook: Dark Web, Ransomware, and Hacktivism Trends
items.summary:
France’s underground cyber threat activity has surged more than fourfold in two years, driven largely by stolen credentials, infostealer logs, ransomware, and pro-Russian hacktivism. CloudSEK’s latest report reveals how government bodies, financial institutions, and smaller organisations are becoming increasingly exposed to a fast-growing cybercrime economy.
Authors : Abhishek Mathew

items.title: Tomorrowland 2026, Belgium: People of Tomorrow, Targets of Today
items.summary:
Tomorrowland 2026 sold out fast, and scammers moved faster. CloudSEK uncovered a dozen fake ticket shops and travel sites mimicking the festival, complete with countdown timers and fake "biometric checks." Some sites harvest identity data and payments; others quietly earn commissions. Read the full breakdown of how each scam works.
Authors : Shobhit Mishra

items.title: THE 5060 SIEGE - Industrialized Attacks Against the SIP Telephony Ecosystem
items.summary:
Uncover how an 18-day honeypot captured 15 million automated attacks targeting telephony ecosystems in the "Copy of SIP Honeypot Report.pdf". Download the full report to expose active VoIP fraud networks and access 277,632 recovered attacker passwords.
Authors : Vikas Kundu

items.title: Inside the FortiBleed Open Directory: A Technical Analysis of What the Attacker Left Behind
items.summary:
An exposed attacker server has revealed FortiBleed’s complete operation—from credential harvesting and GPU-powered cracking to network intrusion and access sales. CloudSEK’s analysis separates verified compromises from inflated claims, uncovering what the attackers actually achieved.
Authors :

items.title: Operation Escaneo: Infrastructure Exposure, TTP Analysis, and Attribution Assessment of an Advanced Intrusion Campaign Against Mexican Federal Agencies and Financial Institutions
items.summary:
An exposed attacker server revealed the inner workings of Operation Escaneo—a sophisticated campaign targeting Latin American governments and financial institutions. CloudSEK maps its custom tools, exploitation chain, persistence tactics and suspected links to MexicanMafia. Read the full investigation.
Authors : Koushik Pal

items.title: Bluekit Phishing as a Service (PhaaS)
items.summary:
BlueKit is turning phishing into a subscription business, offering 87 ready-made kits, automated account takeover and stealthy peer-to-peer infrastructure. CloudSEK’s investigation reveals how this mature PhaaS platform helps even low-skilled criminals target banks, cloud services and global brands.
Authors : Gagan Aggarwal

items.title: Chinese Origin Threat Actors Target FIFA World Cup 2026
items.summary:
As the FIFA World Cup 2026 begins, a highly sophisticated, Chinese-origin threat operation is targeting global football fans. Utilizing pixel-perfect website clones, a multi-tenant reseller network, and an active Man-in-the-Middle framework, these actors intercept payment details and bypass SMS-based two-factor authentication in real time to completely compromise accounts. 
Authors : Gagan Aggarwal

items.title: Inside a WooCommerce Payment Skimmer: How Carders Moved From Phishing Pages to Checkout Backdoors
items.summary:
Cybercriminals are now targeting real e-commerce checkout pages, not just fake websites. This report reveals how a WooCommerce skimmer silently steals card details during genuine payments. Read the full report to understand the hidden risk.
Authors : Shobhit Mishra

items.title: How an Unauthenticated MCP Server Led to SSRF, LFI, and AWS Credential Theft
items.summary:
A real-world AIVigil finding from a customer environment. One unprotected AI integration endpoint with no login required. An attacker chained Server-Side Request Forgery, Local File Inclusion, and live AWS credential exfiltration into a potential full infrastructure takeover. This is how it happened, and how AIVigil found it first.
Authors : CloudSEK Editorial

items.title: Hit Wicket: Inside The Expansive Web of Scams Targeting Millions of IPL Fans This Season
items.summary:
CloudSEK’s report exposes a highly sophisticated, seasonal IPL online betting scam ecosystem. Fraudsters deploy clone platforms, celebrity AI deepfakes, and blackhat SEO tactics to exploit government domains and trap unsuspecting fans. Sustained by money mule networks, bulk advertisements, and predatory fake loan apps, this industry intentionally blocks user withdrawals, causing severe financial losses and blackmail.
Authors : Sourajeet Majumder

items.title: Inside a Tor Backed Supply Chain Worm
items.summary:
CloudSEK TRIAD uncovered a sophisticated npm supply chain attack using a typosquatted package, crypto-javascri, to mimic crypto-js. The malware steals npm and GitHub credentials, hijacks maintainer accounts, republishes trojanized packages, and uses Tor-based command-and-control. The campaign targets Linux developer systems and CI/CD environments, creating serious downstream supply chain risk.
Authors : CloudSEK TRIAD

items.title: RedSun: Windows 0day when Defender becomes the attacker
items.summary:
RedSun exposes a critical logic flaw in Windows Defender that allows a standard user to escalate privileges to SYSTEM without admin rights or kernel exploits. By exploiting a missing reparse point validation during file restoration, attackers can redirect Defender’s write operation into System32 and execute arbitrary code. The attack is reliable, unpatched, and affects modern Windows systems with Defender enabled, making it a serious security concern.
Authors : CloudSEK TRIAD
